title: The auditory brainstem response to natural speech is not affected by selective attention
description: EEG recordings from three experiments investigating whether selective attention to natural speech modulates the auditory brainstem response and cortical responses. Experiments 1 and 2 used diotic and dichotic presentation of two competing audiobooks with attention directed to one narrator, while Experiment 3 used passive listening to audiobook stimuli from a previous study. Simultaneous cortical (32-channel active) and subcortical (bipolar passive, with eardrum electrodes in a subset of participants) recordings are provided in BIDS format.
methods_description: Participants listened to 64 s (Exp 1, 2) or ~117 s (Exp 3) audiobook trials in a soundproof room and were cued to attend to one narrator, or to ignore the audio in the passive experiment. EEG was recorded at 25 kHz using a 32-channel active montage for cortical responses and a 2-channel passive bipolar montage (FCz to earlobes) for subcortical responses. Cortical data were downsampled to 1 kHz and subcortical data to 10 kHz. Stimulus triggers were corrected for insert earphone tubing delay.
